stats.fact: GitHub Copilot Free costs $0 and includes 2,000 completions per month, access to selected models, and Copilot CLI; GitHub describes it as a no-credit-card getting-started plan.
GitHub Docs says Copilot Free includes up to 2,000 code completions plus an allowance of GitHub AI Credits, with limited chat and agent usage for individual developers.
Google says Gemini Code Assist for individuals has a quota of 6,000 requests per day, or 180,000 per month, for requests such as code generation and completion.
Google's Gemini Code Assist FAQ states the individual free version is available for personal Gmail accounts and does not require a Google Cloud project.
Amazon Q Developer's perpetual Free Tier provides 50 agentic chat interactions per month and up to 1,000 lines of code transformation per month.
AWS pricing lists Amazon Q Developer Free at $0 and Amazon Q Developer Pro at $19 per user per month, making the free tier the relevant under-$5 option.
Windsurf's 2026 pricing announcement says Free, Pro, and Teams moved away from credits to daily and weekly usage allowances; paid overages are consumed at API pricing.
OpenCode positions itself as an open-source AI coding agent with free models included and support for connecting models from providers such as Claude, GPT, and Gemini.
Aider reports 44K GitHub stars, 6.8M installs, and 15B tokens per week, showing strong open-source terminal-agent adoption.
Continue's Visual Studio Marketplace listing describes it as a free, open-source AI code agent and shows more than 3.3M installs.
Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey found 84% of respondents use or plan to use AI tools in development, with 51% of professional developers using AI tools daily.
Stack Overflow reported in February 2026 that only 29% of 2025 survey respondents trusted AI output, down 11 percentage points from 2024, making verification a core buying criterion.
Sonar's State of Code report says developers estimate 42% of their committed or contributed code is currently AI-generated or AI-assisted, projected to rise by more than half by 2027.

angles: Budget truth: under $5/month mostly means free tiers, open-source agents with local models, or BYOK workflows using free model quotas; most polished paid plans start around $10-$20/month.
Rank by real constraints: monthly completions, chat/agent limits, model access, IDE support, privacy posture, and whether the tool can edit multiple files safely.
Use a stack, not one tool: combine Gemini Code Assist for high-volume IDE assistance, GitHub Copilot Free for VS Code/GitHub-native suggestions, and OpenCode or Aider for terminal agent workflows.
Free is not unlimited: explain what happens when a quota runs out, which features are limited, and when a paid plan becomes cheaper than context switching.
Trust gap angle: free tools are useful, but the article should emphasize tests, diffs, dependency review, and human approval because developer trust in AI output is falling.
Local-first angle: Aider, OpenCode, Continue, and Zed/BYOK can be effectively free with local Ollama-style models, but quality depends on hardware and model choice.
Avoid misleading picks: Tabnine, Cursor Pro, Claude Code subscriptions, Zed Pro, and Amazon Q Pro are important comparisons but are not under-$5 ongoing options for most users.
